earlier_scan.source_named: Silva Martins 2007 'Revisão da família lingüística Kamakã' (UnB MA thesis, PDF read from repositorio.unb.br) is a comparative lexical revision of old wordlists — no acento/stress statement; language extinct, wordlist-only records.

new_statements.quote: 1. O último acento é o tônico: kupã, kópá, i. é, kupã’, kópá’. Os outros se referem ao timbre, como em port.: ã, nasal; à, aberto, não final; á, aberto e final; ó [ɔ], é [ɛ], abertos; ô [o], ê [e], fechados. não havendo acento na última sílaba, o vocábulo é paroxítono: kóbéni, não kóbénı́. Às vezes também a é aberto, não final, e representou-se por á. 2. Às vezes, colocou-se acento agudo após a última vogal já acentuada; é para indicar a tônica: kitxiãkü’.
new_statements.translation: 1. The last accent mark is the tonic (stress) one: kupã, kópá, i.e. kupã’, kópá’. The other marks refer to vowel quality, as in Portuguese: ã nasal; à open, non-final; á open and final; ó [ɔ], é [ɛ] open; ô [o], ê [e] close. When there is no accent on the last syllable, the word is paroxytone: kóbéni, not kóbénı́. Sometimes a is also open, non-final, and was written á. 2. Sometimes an acute was placed after an already-marked final vowel; this is to indicate the stressed syllable: kitxiãkü’.
new_statements.citation: Guérios, R. F. Mansur. 1945. Estudos sôbre a língua Camacã. Arquivos do Museu Paranaense 4: 291-320 — pronunciation key, as quoted verbatim in Grahl, João Arthur Pugsley. 2009. Kamakã em Prolog: possibilidades de análise de uma língua de tradição oral morta. MA thesis, UFPR, pp. 59-60.
new_statements.locator: Grahl 2009, §3.3.1 'O corpus', pp. 59-60 (block quotation of Guérios 1945's 'chave para sua pronunciação', items 1-2)
new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule is stated; the only first-hand information is Guérios' transcription convention for his c.1940 semi-speaker wordlist: each word is stressed either on the final syllable (marked with a final acute/apostrophe, e.g. kupã’, kópá’, txaköü’, hâmã’) or, when the final syllable is unmarked, on the penult (kóbéni). Stress thus falls within a final two-syllable window and must be read off item by item; many recorded forms are oxytone (dakó, nanká, södá) but penult forms also occur.
new_statements.exceptions: None as such; Guérios himself warns (quoted p.62 and in the 1948 letters) that the same word was recorded 'ora com um acento, ora com outro, e ora sem nada', i.e. accent placement varied between repetitions; informant Aratimbó was a rememberer whose Portuguese-influenced pronunciation Nimuendajú distrusted.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation forms elicited from a single semi-speaker (Manoel Aratimbó, c.1940); convention for reading diacritics, not a phonological analysis. Wied 1821 independently notes final a/o are 'abruptly broken off' and marks accent ad hoc on some items.
new_statements.identity_note: All material refers to Kamakã proper (Kamakan, kama1372; Guérios' and Nimuendajú's informants at Posto Paraguaçu, Bahia, c.1938-1940) and to the closely related Mongoyó/Kotoxó lists of Wied and Martius, which Martins 2007 treats as one language distinct from Kamakã sensu stricto (Kotoxó = koto1257? within Kamakanan); Menien and Masakará are separate Kamakanan varieties. The stress key concerns Guérios' Kamakã (Aratimbó) list only.

sources.citation: Grahl, João Arthur Pugsley. 2009. Kamakã em Prolog: possibilidades de análise de uma língua de tradição oral morta. MA thesis, Universidade Federal do Paraná. 135 pp.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Phonology section (3.3, pp.58-68) covers segment inventory, minimal pairs and OT syllabification only; no stress analysis of its own. On pp.59-60 it reproduces verbatim Guérios (1945)'s pronunciation key, item 1: an acute on the last syllable marks it as tonic; with no accent on the last syllable the word is paroxytone (e.g. kóbéni). Anexo B pp.123-124 is a facsimile of Guérios' corpus, too low-resolution to read.

sources.citation: D'Angelis, Wilmar da R., Carla M. Cunha & Aryon D. Rodrigues. 2002. Bibliografia das línguas Macro-Jê. Campinas: IEL-Unicamp.
sources.note: Bibliography only; Kamakã index lists Loukotka 1932, Guérios 1945c (Estudos sobre a língua Camacã, Arq. Mus. Paranaense 4:291-320) and Wied.

sources.citation: Nikulin, Andrey. 2020. Proto-Macro-Jê: um estudo reconstrutivo. Doctoral thesis, Universidade de Brasília. 595 pp.
sources.note: Treats Kamakã family only lexically (cites material 'tal como aparece nas fontes'); in the phonology chapter states 'Não abordaremos a família Kamakã'. Discusses stress for Rikbáktsa etc. but nothing for Kamakã.

sources.citation: Martins, Andérbio Márcio Silva. 2009. Um estudo comparativo-lexical das famílias Kamakã e Purí. In S. L. B. Braggio & S. Martins Filho (eds.), Línguas e culturas Macro-Jê, 231-238. Goiânia: Vieira.
Martins, Andérbio Márcio Silva. 2007. Revisão da família lingüística Kamakã proposta por Chestmir Loukotka. MA thesis, Universidade de Brasília. 89 pp.
sources.note: Comparative lexical/phonological revision of 19th-c. wordlists plus Guérios 1945; ch.3 'Observações sobre a grafia' discusses only segmental spelling conventions of Martius/Wied/French collectors. No word 'acento'/'tônica' anywhere; silent on stress.

sources.citation: Mattoso Câmara Jr., J. 1959. A obra lingüística de Curt Nimuendajú. Rio de Janeiro: Museu Nacional.
sources.note: Only notes that the 1948 letters contain 'considerações sôbre a fonética Kamakan'; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt & R. F. Mansur Guérios. 1948. Cartas etnolingüísticas. Revista do Museu Paulista n.s. 2: 207-241.
sources.note: 1945 letters debating Kamakã phonetics (Guérios' semi-speaker informant Aratimbó vs. Nimuendajú's 1938 informant Jacinta Grayirá): consonant clusters, reliability; Guérios cites forms with final stress mark (hâmã', txaköü'); Nimuendajú writes the ethnonym Kamakã'. No rule about stress position.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1932. La familia lingüística Kamakan del Brasil. Revista del Instituto de Etnología de la Universidad Nacional de Tucumán 2: 493-524.
sources.note: p.498 'Fonética': consonant/vowel inventory compiled from old wordlists; on accent only the notational remark 'Las vocales acentuadas están indicadas por un acento, las nasales por una tilde'. No statement of stress position.

Section IV 'Langue' (p.~953): 'La langue des Camacans est peu harmonieuse; elle abonde de sons nasaux et gutturaux, et de plus les Indiens coupent brusquement la fin des mots', followed by a wordlist compiled from Martius etc. Nothing on accent.

sources.citation: Wied-Neuwied, Maximilian Prinz zu. 1821. Reise nach Brasilien in den Jahren 1815 bis 1817, Bd. 2 (Anhang II.7: Sprachproben der Camacans oder Mongoyós in der Capitania da Bahia, pp. 327 ff.). Frankfurt a. M.: Brönner.
sources.note: Introductory Anmerkung: many gutturals; 'a und o sind die gewöhnlichen Endungen der Worte, werden aber äusserst kurz abgebrochen, als wenn der Sprecher hier plötzlich den Ton aufhielte'; individual entries carry ad hoc notes ('hai der Accent', 'kiua laut mit Accent', 'ohne besonderen Accent'). No general stress statement.
